title: Processing Materials
summary: Properties and uses of wood, metals and plastics, processing methods (cutting, shaping, joining and finishing), recycling plastics, and protecting materials from deterioration.

notes.text: **Processing** means changing raw materials into useful products by **cutting**, **shaping**, **joining** and **finishing** them. Choosing the right material depends on its **properties**.

rows: Wood (timber)
**Hardwood** from broad-leaved trees (oak, kiaat, meranti); **softwood** from conifers (pine); **manufactured boards** (plywood, chipboard, MDF)
Strong, easy to work, renewable, good insulator, attractive
Ferrous metals (contain iron)
Steel, cast iron, stainless steel
Very strong and hard; most rust (except stainless steel); magnetic
Non-ferrous metals (no iron)
Aluminium, copper, brass, zinc, gold
Do not rust; aluminium is light; copper is an excellent conductor
Thermoplastics
PET (cooldrink bottles), polythene (plastic bags), PVC (pipes), acrylic (Perspex)
Can be softened by heating and reshaped many times; can be recycled
Thermosetting plastics
Melamine (plates, kitchen tops), Bakelite (pot handles, plugs), epoxy resin
Set permanently when heated once; heat resistant; cannot be remoulded

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: **Thermo**plastics soften with heat again and again (like chocolate). **Thermosetting** plastics are set once and then char or burn if heated again (like baking a cake).

rows: Measuring and marking
Steel rule, try square, marking gauge, scriber (for metal), pencil (for wood)
Cutting
Tenon saw and coping saw (wood), hacksaw (metal), snips (sheet metal), craft knife
Shaping
Files, sandpaper, chisels, planes; bending acrylic with a strip heater; moulding
Joining
Nails, screws, glue (wood glue, epoxy), nuts and bolts, rivets, soldering and welding (metal), wood joints such as butt, lap and dowel joints
Finishing
Sanding, painting, varnishing, oiling, polishing, galvanising, powder-coating
Wood
Rot from moisture, termites and borer beetles, warping and cracking in the sun
Paint, varnish, wood preservative (e.g. creosote), treated timber
Iron and steel
Rust (needs oxygen and water)
Paint, oil, galvanising with zinc, plastic coating, using stainless steel
Plastics
Become brittle and fade in UV sunlight
UV stabilisers in the plastic, paint, keeping them shaded

notes.text: Most plastics are made from **oil** (a non-renewable resource) and take hundreds of years to break down, polluting land and oceans. Plastics are marked with a **recycling code** (a number from 1 to 7 inside a triangle of arrows) so they can be sorted. Recycled PET bottles can be made into fibres for clothing, carpets and new bottles.

items: **Reduce**: carry a reusable shopping bag; avoid unnecessary packaging.
**Reuse**: use containers again for storage or projects.
**Recycle**: sort waste and take it to a recycling depot or buy-back centre.

questions.prompt: Why are pot handles made from a thermosetting plastic such as Bakelite?
questions.memo:
✓ It is heat resistant and does not soften when hot (1)
✓ It is a poor conductor of heat, so the handle stays cool / safe to hold (1)

questions.prompt: Give TWO ways to protect an outdoor wooden bench from deterioration.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): paint; varnish; wood preservative; use treated timber; oil

questions.prompt: Explain THREE problems that plastics cause for the environment.
questions.memo: Any three (1 each): made from non-renewable oil; take hundreds of years to break down; litter on land; ocean pollution harming marine life; release toxic fumes when burnt

questions.prompt: Why is copper used for electrical wires?
questions.memo:
✓ It is an excellent conductor of electricity (1)
✓ It is ductile (can be drawn into wires) and does not rust (1)
